In the CL breakout, I would like to discuss plans for the next Hegota devnet for the CL.

My proposal is the following:

* Aim to launch the next devnet October 28th with at least 3 clients.
* Name it `heze-devnet-0` instead of `focil-devnet-2`.
* Include FOCIL + all currently CFI'd features (8015, 8198, 8365).
* If that's too much, make 8198 optional by keeping 12 second slots.

There are two discord threads on this topic with some extra information.

* [`allcoredevs - We should take a look at scoping`](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1557047083939143701)
* [`consensus-dev - devnet scoping for heze`](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1557442447074787438)

> In the CL breakout, I would like to discuss plans for the next Hegota devnet for the CL.
...

I think we should keep devnet scoping related discussions (which leads to SFI) in the general section + ACDC. Many impact ELs as well.

> > In the CL breakout, I would like to discuss plans for the next Hegota devnet for the CL.
> > ...    
>     
> I think we should keep devnet scoping related discussions (which leads to SFI) in the general section + ACDC. Many impact ELs as well.

Sure. We can discuss this in the shared session.

> * 
> * Include FOCIL + all currently CFI'd features (8015, 8198, 8365).

happy with doing CFI features (including quick slots) from our (teku) perspective. would be helpful to get a branch name to use tonight for whatever is decided.

I would like to bring up https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/627 on the CL breakout again, it's the last Gloas Beacon API PR. Since last week I've added additional motivation for it in [this PR comment](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/627#issuecomment-6012901023), and there's also a [thread](https://ptb.discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1556640385789591564) (CL->#apis) up on Discord if people prefer to chime in there. This endpoint should not be a lot of work for CL client teams since they'd only need to implement the Beacon API endpoint, and not the VC side of things.

If it makes people more comfortable, I'd be happy to tag this endpoint as `Experimental`.

I want to discuss the min specs for Glamsterdam. Current specs are https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7870

The 500MB/s seq r/w is too slow for Glamsterdam. We increase 24->64KiB contract size and the gas limit from 60 -> 200 Mgas, and increase account read cost from 2600 to 3000. This itself makes the max amount of bytes read (EVM only, so non other important tasks like MPT node reading) increase by a factor of ~8. The 500 MB/s is too slow.

We should discuss how to address this and if every fork should have new min specs and we thus create a new EIP and link this to the fork. If the min specs dont change, we do not change the min specs EIP (number). For Fusaka (and thus retroactively also older forks) this is thus EIP-7870.

See: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12490

Note, the idea is to move this EIP to Final and not Living like EIP-7870.
